1  critical  Google does not currently require 2-step verification for these accounts (Workspace)
   [workspace.two_step_not_enforced]
   Subject       /Sales (org_unit /sales)
   You declared  engagement.yaml access.mfa[0]: Operator declaration at access.mfa[0]
   Observed      g000008 (12:00, as unknown): Google reports that 2-step verification is not
                 currently required for 2 active accounts in unit /Sales (isEnforcedIn2Sv: false).
                 Enrollment, as Google reports it: 1 not enrolled, 1 enrolled, 0 unknown. Not
                 enrolled: admin@example.com. Enrolled: carol@example.com. For these accounts,
                 Google reports that 2-step verification is not currently enforced. Enrollment,
                 counted above, is a separate flag: a user who enrolled can still turn it off while
                 Google does not require it. scheck did not assess organizational-unit policy, grace
                 periods or protection provided by another sign-in service. Review these accounts
                 and the current Admin console settings yourself, or with whoever administers your
                 Workspace.
   Concluded from request:g000008, declared:access.mfa[0]
   Severity      critical: base high, +1 contradiction (access.mfa[0])
   Why here      You declared that every account must use 2-step verification in this tenant, so
                 this ranks one step higher.
   Not checked   Whether these people sign in to Google through another identity provider, for
                 example Okta or Microsoft Entra, that requires a second factor; if so, Google not
                 requiring its own 2-step verification may be expected for them, and the raise above
                 may not apply. scheck did not read that service or Google's single sign-on
                 settings. Super administrators normally sign in to Google directly and need
                 Google's 2-step verification regardless.
   Fix           In the Admin console, open Security → Authentication → 2-step verification. Check
                 which setting applies to these accounts' organizational unit or groups, and turn on
                 enforcement with a short new-user enrollment period. Tell users before the
                 enforcement date so nobody is locked out. Prefer security keys or passkeys for
                 administrators and for people with access to production or customer data. If people
                 sign in to Google through another identity provider, confirm it requires a second
                 factor for these accounts. Run scheck again to confirm that Google reports them as
                 required.

2  high  An administrator has not enrolled in 2-step verification (Workspace)
   [workspace.admin_without_two_step]
   Subject       admin@example.com (account admin@example.com)
   Observed      g000008 (12:00, as unknown): admin@example.com: super administrator (isAdmin:
                 true); isEnrolledIn2Sv: false.
   Observed      g000010 (12:00, as unknown): admin@example.com: super administrator (isAdmin:
                 true); isEnrolledIn2Sv: false.
   Severity      high
   Why here      This is the standard rating for the observed access or settings.
   Fix           Have this administrator enroll in 2-step verification now, preferably with a
                 security key or passkey. For a break-glass account, register two hardware keys and
                 store them apart. If the role is not needed, remove it or suspend the account until
                 it is enrolled. Then require 2-step verification for administrators in the Admin
                 console (Security → Authentication → 2-step verification) so it cannot be turned
                 off.
